name: Clear Fluorite Green
lede: Clear Fluorite Green is a light, muted green named for the transparent green form of fluorite, a mineral prized by collectors, recorded by Ridgway in 1912.

sections.title: A collector's mineral
sections.body:
Our library traces Clear Fluorite Green to fluorite, a mineral that forms transparent, often green or purple crystals, with Ridgway's 1912 standards placing it on plate XXXII, hue 33′′, tone b, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classing a close match as light yellowish green, 5.3 units of ΔE away [1].

The nearest everyday name on file is [[sage]], 5.8 units off, with [[malachite-green]], another mineral name, listed as the closer library neighbor [1]. In LCH terms it is light and moderately chromatic: lightness 75, chroma 31, hue 127 degrees [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Clear Fluorite Green in only 50, as photographed[2]. It is used far more than chance by Vincent van Gogh and Edvard Munch, over 38 times each painter's own baseline, and appears in van Gogh's *[[painting:nga-72328|Roses]]* of 1890 at 44 percent coverage and in his *Roulin's Baby* of 1888 [2]. Its use across the archive also skews heavily toward Norway, nearly 16 times the expected rate, and peaks in the 1910s, in 5 of 523 paintings [2].
